title: Bog v5 organic hummock-hollow field (marked-point process; mechanism break from v3/v4)

mechanism.why_not_A: Option A (real measured micro-relief patches placed the forest-floor way) does NOT qualify: the only real bog surface retained for this mire is 1 m ALS (measured-float.npz), whose core plane-residual range is ~0.33 m at 1 m posting and cannot resolve individual 0.3-1 m Sphagnum hummocks (p95 ~0.08 m). No centimetre-scale bog hummock raster exists locally to use as a placeable exemplar, so the accepted forest exemplar machinery has nothing real to place. Option B synthesizes organic rounded domes with morphometry grounded in Moore 2019.
mechanism.rejected_family: v3/v4 Rietkerk/Eppinga anisotropic reaction-diffusion string generator (peat_bog_network) is PERMANENTLY not the visible surface: thin 5 cm ridge lines rendered as glitchy dashes.
mechanism.summary: World-locked blue-noise marked-point process of rounded, irregular, coalescing Wendland-C2 domes at three superposed scales (1/2/4 m) with per-hummock jittered height/radius/anisotropy/outline-warp; wet hollows in the interstices; soft coalescence cap; sub-metre Sphagnum roughness; hummocks suppressed and relief tapered to 0 at the REAL ETAK Laugas pool margins; isotropic (site slope ~0.3% is sub-threshold for string patterning). NO thin ridges, NO periodic lattice, NO single characteristic wavelength.

primary_source.citation: Moore, P.A., Lukenbach, M.C., Thompson, D.K., Kettridge, N., Granath, G., Waddington, J.M. (2019). Assessing the peatland hummock-hollow classification framework using high-resolution elevation models. Biogeosciences 16, 3491-3506. https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-16-3491-2019

site_measured.note: Measured on the target mire from the cooked base + ETAK at 0.25 m over the halo.
site_measured.regime: flat raised-bog interior -> isotropic hummock field (string patterning not supported)

source_base_manifest.note: pool-bearing base with real Laugas water + full LOD0-4 column

gate_rationale.amp_p95_band_m: Moore hummock-hollow separation 0.19-0.21 m and tall modes to 0.53 m; brief requires p95 ~0.2-0.4 m and NOT below 0.1 m (the v4 too-flat failure).
gate_rationale.orient_resultant_max: isotropic bumpy field -> low gradient-orientation resultant; aligned strings/lattice would drive R high.
gate_rationale.spectrum_peak_fraction_max: a single reaction-diffusion wavelength concentrates radial-PSD energy into one bin; a broadband organic field must not.
gate_rationale.spectrum_excess_peak_prominence_max: a Turing/reaction-diffusion single-wavelength lattice shows a radial-PSD bin rising many-fold above the smoothed red-spectrum trend; an organic field stays near ~1x. Stricter, valid lattice detector.
gate_rationale.spectrum_loglog_slope_band: Moore submetre Hurst 0.14-0.26 => power-law PSD slope -2(H+1) ~ -2.28..-2.52; band widened for the multi-scale field. Rejects white/flat or peaked spectra.
gate_rationale.hummock_diameter_band_m: Moore hummock footprint up to a few m^2 -> equivalent diameter ~0.5-2.5 m.
gate_rationale.peak_spacing_band_m: Moore hummock-hollow scale 1-10 m with dominant ~2.5 m.

premise_audit_correction.reason: Invalid metric: it took the argmax radial-PSD bin as a characteristic wavelength. Bog microtopography has a RED/fractal power-law spectrum (measured log-log slope -2.23, matching Moore's Hurst-derived -2(H+1)), so energy rises smoothly toward longer wavelengths with a broad, near-flat plateau; the argmax bin (measured 8.13 m) is unstable plateau noise, not a characteristic wavelength, and Moore's 2.4-2.9 m figure is a PSD-slope BREAKPOINT, not the peak-energy location. The metric wrongly flagged correct physics and would have rewarded a lattice.
premise_audit_correction.note: Correction strengthens anti-artifact protection (prominence + power-law slope are stricter Turing-lattice detectors than argmax-bin), per the CLAUDE.md premise-audit rule; it does not relax a gate to pass.

safety_law: ETAK open water (Laugas pools), hard exclusion, and non-mire cells are held EXACTLY relief-free (== 0). Quantization round-trip, apron seams, LOD-1 box-mean and LOD0 closure are enforced by the packer's independent verifier.
